intended_object: A sequential space: a topological space in which every sequentially closed set (one containing all limits of convergent sequences of its points) is closed. Taken from the docstring and the name.
explanation: `IsSeqClosed s` says that whenever every `x n ∈ s` and `x` tends to `p`, then `p ∈ s`. This is the standard notion of a sequentially closed set, and it does not assume that limits are unique. The class requires every sequentially closed set to be closed, which is exactly the textbook definition of a sequential space; the converse holds in every topological space. It is stated for arbitrary topological spaces, the natural generality, and it is Mathlib's canonical definition, so there is no separate counterpart to cite.
